speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a rash on your scalp and forehead; can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the patient's age and the scaly, erythematous rash worsening in cold weather, I suspect this could be eczema or potentially psoriasis given the family history. Have you noticed any family history of atopy, such as asthma or hay fever, in addition to the father's psoriasis?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis. The patient's age (3 months), location (scalp/forehead), specific appearance (greasy yellow scales), and exacerbation by cold weather are classic presentations for this condition, distinguishing it from psoriasis (dry, silvery scales) or eczema (typically dry, itchy). No further tests are required.
